question.text: How much will Crude Oil Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 9 - Nov 20)
question.resolution_criteria:
Each subquestion will resolve as the difference between the percent total price return of [Crude Oil Futures (CL)](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CL%3DF/history/) and that of [S\&P 500 Futures (ES)](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ES%3DF/history/) for the corresponding biweekly period, according to Yahoo Finance data.

Specifically, each subquestion will resolve as CL\_return - ES\_return.

Returns will be calculated as follows: If P₀ is the Close price of a company stock on the last trading day or half-day *before* the start of the period and P₁ is the Close price of the stock on the last trading day *of* the designated period, the percentage return will be calculated as:

$$
 \text{return} = 100 \times \frac{P1 - P0}{P0}
$$
question.fine_print:
* If ES outperforms CL, the corresponding subquestion will resolve as a negative number.
* If Yahoo Finance delays or ceases reporting these data or if it reports them in error, Metaculus might use alternative credible sources to resolve this question.

***

For example, for the period Jun 9 - Jun 20, the subquestion would resolve based on the following calculations:

CL\_P₀ \= 64.58 (the Close price on Jun 6)

CL\_P₁ \= 74.93 (the Close price on Jun 20)

CL\_return \= 100 × (74.93 - 64.58) / 64.58 \= 16.0266

ES\_P₀ \= 6,006.75 (the Close price on Jun 6)

ES\_P₁ \= 6,010.21 (the Close price on Jun 20)

ES\_return \= 100 × (6,010.21 - 6,006.75) / 6,006.75 \= 0.0576

And the resolution would be 16.0266 - 0.0576 \= **15.9690** percentage points (pp).

# Research brief: CL minus ES return, Nov 9 to Nov 20, 2026

## 1. Resolution source

- 2026-11-02: Yahoo lists CL=F as the "Crude Oil Dec 26" contract. Recent closes: Oct 30: 104.12, Oct 29: 102.00, Oct 28: 102.78, Oct 23: 103.27, Oct 20: 101.79. The Nov 2 figure was 96.50, but the market was still open, so it may be an intraday price rather than the close. [Yahoo CL=F](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CL%3DF/history/)
- 2026-11-02: Yahoo lists ES=F as the "E-Mini S&P 500 Dec 26" contract. Closes: Oct 30: 7,614.00, Oct 29: 7,754.25, Oct 21: 7,800.25. The Nov 2 figure of 7,640.75 is also intraday. [Yahoo ES=F](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ES%3DF/history/)
- **Contract roll risk:** under CME rules, the Dec 2026 WTI contract should stop trading around Nov 20, which is my own calculation. Yahoo already showed the Dec contract by Oct 20, which is when I calculate the Nov contract expired. If CL=F switches to the January contract before or on Nov 20, the series could drop mechanically by roughly the Dec/Jan backwardation. In October that spread was about $3/bbl, around 3%, though the numbers are poorly sourced. [commodity-board](https://commodity-board.com/wti-marches-above-100-while-curve-remains-steeply-backwardated), [commodity-board](https://commodity-board.com/crude-oil-rally-steepens-backwardation-as-brent-wti-spread-widens)

## 4. Base rates
- **CL, from the code baseline:** over 12 trading days from 96.51, the price percentiles are p5 85.5, p10 88.0, p25 92.7, p50 97.1, p75 101.6, p90 107.3, p95 114.6. As returns, that is roughly -11% at p5, -9% at p10, -4% at p25, +0.6% at the median, +5% at p75, +11% at p90 and +19% at p95.
- **Daily volatility is currently high:** CL moved by 2% to 4% on most days in late October, for example -4.6% on Oct 21 and +3.8% on Oct 23. A peace deal or an escalation could move it 10% or more in a single fortnight.
- **ES:** I estimate a typical biweekly standard deviation of about 2% to 3%. This is a rough judgement, not a calculation. Recently ES fell about 2.4% from Oct 21 to Nov 2.
- **The spread:** CL dominates the variance of the difference. The middle 80% of outcomes plausibly spans roughly -11 to +11 pp, before any roll effect.
- **Correlation:** in this war regime, oil and stocks have tended to move in opposite directions. Oil falls on peace hopes while stocks rise, as on Nov 2. That widens the spread distribution.
- I could not access the question's Google spreadsheet of past returns.
